Issued at 259 AM EDT Tue Oct 6 2026

Today-Tonight...Ongoing showers and a few storms around 2 AM this 
morning are forecast to diminish and push offshore through daybreak. 
However, a few showers will remain possible through the morning 
hours, mainly from Orlando northward, as a weak front settles in 
over the area. This front is forecast to stall across central 
Florida today where it will linger through mid-week, maintaining 
deep moisture over the peninsula. 

Near record PWATs for the date today, forecast near 2.3-2.4". Deep 
moisture and lift along the front will support multiple rounds of 
widespread showers and embedded thunderstorms. PoPs 60-85% are 
forecast area-wide through this afternoon. However, additional 
rounds of precipitation will be possible during the evening and 
overnight hours, with PoPs remaining up to 40-60% through midnight. 
It is difficult to pick out an area for the heaviest rainfall today, 
with 90th percentile 24 hour accumulations 2.5-3" for nearly all of 
the forecast area through tonight. Therefore, all of east central 
Florida is under a Marginal Risk (1/4) for excessive rainfall today. 
Minor flooding will be possible in areas that receive multiple 
rounds of showers and storms. A few strong storms, capable of wind 
gusts to near 45 mph, will be possible, but limited instability will 
hamper thunderstorm development overall. 

Light and variable flow is forecast today, with highs limited to the 
lower to mid-80s north of Orlando. A low pressure system looks to 
develop along the front tonight offshore from the Southeast US, 
though winds are not forecast to respond until Wednesday.
Overnight lows remain in the 70s, with high humidity.

Wednesday-Thursday...The stationary front remains stalled near or 
across the forecast area through mid-week. Deep moisture will 
continue to support widespread coverage of showers and scattered 
embedded lightning storms, as PWATs linger near record for the 
dates. PoPs 75-85% are forecast area-wide, with multiple rounds of 
convection through the day generated by lift along the boundary.
PoPs up to 60-70% also linger through the evening and overnight 
hours, making for an overall soggy week. Widespread accumulations of 
1-2" are forecast through Thursday, though pockets of amounts near 
or in excess of 4" are possible, with at least a 40% chance of 
exceeding 2" across the entire area. At least portions of east 
central Florida are highlighted in a Marginal Risk (1/4) for 
excessive rainfall through Thursday. Locations that see multiple 
rounds of heavy rainfall will be at risk for minor flooding. May 
need to monitor the Volusia coast in particular for training bands, 
with SW flow aloft and strengthening onshore flow at the surface.

Warm temperatures aloft (-4 to -5 C at 500mb) will limit the threat 
for strong storms. However, a few gusts to 45 mph cannot be ruled 
out in the strongest storms. Lightning may be limited overall 
through the daytime hours, though, as high coverage of clouds limits 
instability. The low pressure developing offshore from the Southeast 
US coast strengthens Wednesday, before broadening Thursday. This 
will lead to breezy to windy conditions north of the front 
(generally from near Cape Canaveral northward) along the coast. 
Onshore winds along the Volusia County coast look to increase to 15-
20 mph, with gusts 25-30 mph Wednesday afternoon and evening. Winds 
slacken Thursday, but remain breezy along the Volusia and Space 
Coasts, with gusts 20-25 mph. Elsewhere, winds remain 10-15 mph or 
less. High coverage of showers and storms will keep high 
temperatures in the 80s, with muggy lows in the 70s.

Friday-Tuesday...All eyes late week and into this weekend turn to 
the Gulf, where an area of low pressure is being monitored for 
tropical development. While the forecast remains uncertain, ridging 
over the central US looks to shift eastward Friday into Saturday, 
allowing the low to move ashore somewhere along the northern Gulf 
coast. Locally, this could mean little for the overall pattern. 
While this system may be able to drag the stationary front 
northward, southerly flow over the Florida peninsula would maintain 
deep moisture over the area. Currently, rain chances remain above 
normal (60-80%) Friday and this weekend, before slightly drier air 
lowers rain chances somewhat into early next week. Breezy onshore 
winds return Friday and Saturday, as the pressure gradient tightens 
between the low and ridging to the north. Temperatures creep up a 
few degrees each day, especially as cloud cover diminishes. Highs 
return to the upper 80s, with muggy conditions leading to heat 
indices in the 90s to lower 100s.
